content:
Mike B: ran perf (cpu) during a batch build on ded-01, seeing long PyEval_RestoreThread / mutex stalls. dropping notes.
Anya K: which binary/kernel? is this on the new scheduler flags?
Mike B: kernel is linux-5.15, runtime build: rwinf/1.8.2. commit: a3f9b. quick perf top dump:
```
    22.3%  python3  [.] PyEval_RestoreThread
    15.1%  runtime  [.] dispatcher_handle_batch
     8.7%  runtime  [.] BatchBuilder::append_token
     5.2%  libc     [.] __pthread_mutex_lock
```
Devon R: interesting — looks like mutex contention in the batching path. did you try perf record + flamegraph?
Mike B: yep, perf record -F 99 -g -- python3 -m workload.runner
perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > batch-flame.svg
attached small SVG.
Serena L: could be GIL + our spin-wait in dispatcher. try enabling per-worker batching (--worker-batch) and re-run.
Mike B: re-ran with --worker-batch=1k, latency improved 9-12%, but CPU tail still noisy. stack traces show more time in memcpy near K/V copy.
Anya K: can you run perfetto natively for a timeline? we need to see thread hops and wakeups.
Mike B: starting perfetto capture now, will share trace link.
perf-bot: trace capture completed: /traces/1835001234/perfetto.pb
Devon R: next steps: instrument dispatcher to avoid holding GIL while assembling tensors; and consider swapping to lock-free queue for batch building.
Serena L: also add a small C extension for tokenization hotpath to reduce Python boundary crossing.
Mike B: noted. I'll open a tiny RFC with perf outputs and attach flame + perfetto. thanks :thumbsup:
